title: Theo and the Vector
premise: Wendell Fairweather has spent eleven years as the sole human caretaker of Relay Station Vesper, maintaining the automated beacons that keep two rival human fleets from drifting into open war. When the derelict ship Calliope returns from a deep-space fold experiment with its crew aged backward into children, Wendell hides them, fabricating fleet traffic to conceal the anomaly—because the truth of what the fold did could shatter the fragile truce both sides blame on each other. As investigators close in and the children begin remembering fragments of their adult lives, Wendell realizes the lie he's protecting was built on his own family's sacrifice: his sister was aboard the original expedition. In the end, Wendell broadcasts the truth himself, choosing belonging over invisibility, and the two fleets must decide whether shared grief can become shared purpose.
about_author: Mara Nystrom is a former radio operator who spent six years on remote northern stations before turning to fiction full-time. Her work explores loneliness at scale—the quiet heroism of people who keep systems running that no one remembers exist.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A routine maintenance cycle across the relay chain, establishing his solitude, his rituals, and his careful avoidance of fleet politics. He repairs a beacon no one will thank him for. Emotional beat: contentment with a hairline crack of loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: Signal Without a Source
chapters.summary: Wendell detects an unscheduled return vector from deep space—a ship that shouldn't exist anymore. He logs it, hesitates, and almost reports it. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Calliope
chapters.summary: The derelict docks itself. Wendell boards and finds thirty children in cryo-grown bodies wearing adult crew uniforms, including a girl clutching a technician's badge with his family name on it. Emotional beat: vertigo—the impossible made physical.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wendell hides the ship in a dead sensor shadow and invents plausible traffic logs. His POV alternates with brief entries from the Calliope's black box. Emotional beat: the first deliberate lie, and how easily it comes.

chapters.title: Small Voices, Old Eyes
chapters.summary: The children wake fully; they have fragmented adult memories surfacing in dreams. A boy named Ivo recalls the fold accident but not his own name. Emotional beat: tenderness Wendell didn't know he still had capacity for.

chapters.title: The Badge
chapters.summary: Wendell examines the badge: it belonged to his sister Ada, listed dead eleven years ago. Flashbacks reveal she volunteered for the fold project after their parents' deaths. Emotional beat: grief reopened like a wound kept clean too long.

chapters.title: Queries from Meridian
chapters.summary: Fleet Command pings the station about anomalous energy readings. Wendell improvises a solar flare cover story. His hands shake only after he signs off. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into competence.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Silence
chapters.summary: Exposition through intercepted fleet broadcasts: the Concord and the Reach blame each other for the lost expedition, and war talk is rising. Wendell understands the children are proof neither side wants. Emotional beat: the weight of being the only witness.

chapters.title: Ada's Notebook
chapters.summary: Among the recovered effects, Wendell finds Ada's journal describing the fold's true purpose: not travel, but a weapon both fleets secretly funded. Emotional beat: betrayal—the truce he serves is built on a shared crime.

chapters.title: Ivo Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Ivo's memories consolidate; he was the fold engineer and knows the effect is spreading backward along their tethers—they have months before the aging reversal becomes permanent or fatal. Emotional beat: urgency replacing wonder.

chapters.title: The Inspector
chapters.summary: A Concord investigator, Sefa Oyelaran, arrives unannounced for a routine audit. Wendell performs normalcy while hiding thirty heartbeats one deck below. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension; every small talk exchange is a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Hairline Fracture
chapters.summary: A child wanders into view during the audit. Wendell claims she's a stowaway from a freighter; Oyelaran pretends to believe him—and leaves a hidden tracker. Emotional beat: the lie now has a heartbeat and a face.

chapters.title: What the Tracker Hears
chapters.summary: Wendell discovers the device feeding audio to both fleets simultaneously—he realizes Oyelaran works for neither, but for a third faction wanting the war ignited. Emotional beat: paranoia; the station itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Burning the Logs
chapters.summary: Wendell purges eleven years of honest records to build a consistent false history, mourning the erasure of his own past. The children help, treating it like a game until they grasp the stakes. Emotional beat: sacrifice of self to protect others.

chapters.title: The Reach Arrives
chapters.summary: A Reach patrol vessel demands docking rights, citing the same flare report. Two hostile crews will soon share one corridor. Wendell stalls with a fabricated quarantine. Emotional beat: the trap closing from both sides.

chapters.title: Quarantine Theater
chapters.summary: Wendell stages a convincing contamination scenario while Ivo secretly restores the Calliope's fold drive. A Reach officer recognizes the ship's silhouette. Emotional beat: performance under pressure, sweat and improvisation.

chapters.title: Oyelaran Returns
chapters.summary: The inspector comes back with Concord marines, revealing she knows everything and offers Wendell a deal: surrender the children as evidence against the Reach, and live. Emotional beat: temptation—the easy exit that costs his soul.

chapters.title: Ada's Voice
chapters.summary: Wendell plays Ada's final log entry, recovered from the drive: she chose the fold knowing the risk, believing the truth would someday matter more than the fleets' pride. Emotional beat: inheritance—her courage passed to him.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds
chapters.summary: Climax begins: marines breach the station as Ivo charges the fold drive. Wendell triggers the station's master broadcast—every relay, both fleets' channels—streaming the Calliope's black box and Ada's logs. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Everything Speaks at Once
chapters.summary: Both fleets receive the truth mid-standoff; weapons lock, then waver as crews recognize their own lost expedition members among the children. Oyelaran's faction tries to jam the signal; Wendell physically holds the transmitter array together. Emotional beat: chaos cracking open into stunned silence.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the fold effect stabilizes thanks to Ivo's counter-field, but the children will grow up twice, carrying two lives. Both fleets sign a provisional accord at Vesper. Wendell is offered command and refuses. Emotional beat: exhaustion, relief, and the cost tallied honestly.

chapters.title: Home Route
chapters.summary: Resolution: Wendell runs the long route one last time—not alone, but with the children aboard as apprentices, teaching them the beacons. Ada's badge rides on the console. The relays finally carry voices between worlds that speak again. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not found.
